newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to cut jobs in restructuring move.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to cut jobs in restructuring move.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Wednesday it would be reorganising its businesses into autonomous profit centres in a move aimed at cutting management and administration positions by 10 percent.
Lufthansa said in a statement it would be creating a wide-ranging passenger division under which sales, marketing, network management, flight and staff operations would be brought together.
It said the move was a response to the liberalisation of the European air traffic market.
The changes, to take effect from April 1, mark the completion of a restructuring begun in 1994, Lufthansa said in a statement.
The passenger division will be led by a divisional management board which will be responsible for its profitability, the statement said. That board will report to the group management board.
The changes will lead to "greater market proximity, flexibility and homegeneity of leadership," the statement said.
